trigger: vacuous_control_finding.json: frozen_random_projection is a square full-rank (invertible) matrix, so any probe-based metric is invariant to it (the probe absorbs the inverse). Ties measured by probes were forced, not observed.
principle: sort each census comparison by WHAT the metric is. Probe-based metrics (linear/MLP accuracy, transfer, nonlinear-gain) are mathematically invariant to an invertible linear map and their frozen-random tie is vacuous. Distance/robustness metrics are only approximately affected. Trained-shell metrics (continual-learning gain, BWT) depend on input conditioning and are NOT invariant, so their deltas are genuine.

guaranteed_vacuous_ties.why: linear or MLP probe metric; invariant to invertible linear map; delta 0.000 was forced by the control, says nothing about the substrate

entries: c3_prototype_typicality:silhouette_real (distance-ratio, only approximately preserved by a random Gaussian map; tie is weak real evidence of projection-invariance)

genuine_surviving_signal.why: trained SGD continual-learning shell; forgetting depends on input geometry, not linear separability; NOT invariant to an invertible linear map, so the delta is real. Architectural (sparse/gated heads), the corpus's one substrate-touching positive.

conclusion: Of the census's 7 ties, 5 were guaranteed by the vacuous control and 1 more is a ceiling; only the silhouette tie is real (weak) evidence of projection-invariance. The 2 e7_sparse beats survive. The census did NOT establish that the pooled substrate is unspecial for what a probe could not, in principle, distinguish. The substrate question is reopened and moved to substrate_vs_random_features.py / substrate_vs_random_init_vit.py.
